hints: Recall the range of the sine function: $-1 \le \sin\left(\frac{1}{2}x\right) \le 1$.
Find the greatest value when the sine term equals $1$: $y = 2 + 3(1)$.
Find the least value when the sine term equals $-1$: $y = 2 + 3(-1)$.
walkthrough:
Use the fundamental bounds of the sine function:
$$-1 \le \sin\left(\frac{1}{2}x\right) \le 1$$

Determine the greatest value of $y$:
$$\text{Greatest value} = 2 + 3(1) = 5$$

Determine the least value of $y$:
$$\text{Least value} = 2 + 3(-1) = 2 - 3 = -1$$

ai_rubric.Graphs of Trigonometric Functions: States greatest value $= 5$ and least value $= -1$.

walkthrough:
Determine the period and key coordinates for $y = 2 + 3\sin\left(\frac{1}{2}x\right)$ over $[0, 4\pi]$:
$$\text{Period} = \frac{2\pi}{1/2} = 4\pi$$
$$\text{Start}: (0, 2), \quad \text{Max}: (\pi, 5), \quad \text{Midline}: (2\pi, 2), \quad \text{Min}: (3\pi, -1), \quad \text{End}: (4\pi, 2)$$

Sketch one complete sine cycle oscillating between $y = -1$ and $y = 5$ around the horizontal line $y = 2$, showing correct sinusoidal curvature and clearly indicating the maximum ($5$) and minimum ($-1$) on the vertical scale.

ai_rubric.Sketching Trigonometric Graphs: Sketches one complete cycle of sine curve starting at $(0,2)$, with maximum 5 at $x=\pi$ and minimum $-1$ at $x=3\pi$, finishing at $(4\pi,2)$.

hints: Interpret the equation as the intersection of the curve $y = 2 + 3\sin\left(\frac{1}{2}x\right)$ and the straight line $y = 5 - 2x$.
Check values of the straight line: at $x = 0$, $y = 5$; at $x = \pi \approx 3.14$, $y = 5 - 2\pi \approx -1.28 < -1$.
Since the line drops below the minimum value $-1$ for $x > 3$ and never returns, identify how many intersections occur.
walkthrough:
Consider the line $y = 5 - 2x$ alongside the curve $y = 2 + 3\sin\left(\frac{1}{2}x\right)$ on the domain $[0, 4\pi]$:
$$\text{At } x = 0: \quad y_{\text{line}} = 5, \quad y_{\text{curve}} = 2$$
$$\text{At } x = \pi: \quad y_{\text{line}} = 5 - 2\pi \approx -1.28, \quad y_{\text{curve}} = 5$$
Since $y_{\text{line}} > y_{\text{curve}}$ at $x = 0$ and $y_{\text{line}} < y_{\text{curve}}$ at $x = \pi$, the continuous graphs must intersect at least once between $x = 0$ and $x = \pi$.

$$1 \text{ solution}$$

ai_rubric.Intersections of Graphs: Identifies that the line $y=5-2x$ intersects the sine curve exactly once on $0 \le x \le 4\pi$, giving 1 solution.
